question.text: If the coordinates of one end of a diameter of the circle \(x^2+y^2+4 x-8 y+5=0\), is \((2,1)\), the coordinates of the other end is

solution.text:
Hints: \(x^2+y^2+9 x-8 y+5=0\) Centre circle \((-2,4)\)
\(\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{h}+2}{2}=-2 \\ & \mathrm{~h}=-4-2=-6 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{k}+1}{2}=4 \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=7 \\ & (\mathrm{~h}, \mathrm{k}) \rightarrow(-6,7) \end{aligned}\)
